No getter ever calls a phase or a rebuild.
397	
398	**13.5 Snapshot, restore and size (TR-lsg-036).** The Graph's budgets are: `snapshot(ctx)` (building the payload) at most 0.5 ms; the payload at most 32 KB canonical for the MVP ship; `restore` plus `post_restore` at most 2 ms; the canonical bytes byte-identical after restore, all measured on the release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (S3, on the F-MVP fixture at the weld, mid-breach). The kernel's integration-world figures (3 ms snapshot and 10 ms restore for the 32-block world) are the kernel's (TR-cmd-032, ADR-0006 § 1.9); the Graph's share of them must not exceed its own numbers. Container work (canonical encode, hash, `var_to_bytes`) is not in the 0.5 ms: it is ADR-0005's and ADR-0006's and is measured by SAVE-WRK-1. Expected shape, all UNVERIFIED until S3: the snapshot is about 70 `duplicate()` calls and nine small Dictionaries (ADR-0011 probed 0.11 microseconds per 4,096-element column), far inside 0.5 ms; restore is a linear validation over about 70 columns and 600 rows plus a member-by-member copy, then `post_restore` (an `ensure_derived` rebuild, the bucket seeds and the structural invariants). Working split, to be replaced by S3: validation 0.8 ms, copy 0.1 ms, `post_restore` 1.1 ms. If the 32 KB is exceeded the levers are ADR-0011 § 3.11's, in its order, then a request to raise the ceiling with the measurement. The size after the two hook-product columns is about 30.5 KB at the roster (§ 11).
399	
400	**13.6 The Interaction share (TR-interact-038).** Interaction's hook budget is Interaction's and ADR-0017's; what the Graph owes it is that every call it makes is bounded and allocation-free: `check_set_opening_area` and `check_set_valve` are a handful of column reads, an applied M13 is one column write plus one `mark_dirty`, and `GraphView` reads are O(1) getters. 189	
190	**Ledger nesting (ADR-0007 OQ-B).** `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json` is one `section_templates` space with one flat `pairs[]`, exactly the shape ADR-0007 § 3.2 defines, so `LedgerCheck.verify` stays generic and the append-only CI gate needs no second format. Two classes share the space, told apart by **key shape**: a template pair has key `<template_id>`, a room pair has key `<template_id>/<room_key>` (the `/` is illegal inside a snake_case key, so the split is unambiguous). Template ids come from the low part of the declared range and room ids from above a fixed boundary (a `SectionLedgerCheck` in `src/data/sections/`, owned by Layout by review, checks the boundary, that every room pair's prefix is a template pair in the same ledger, and that retiring or dormanting a template does the same to its room pairs: lint `LEDGER_ROOM_ORPHAN`). One entry per `room_key` rather than a nested list keeps `dormant` and `retired_ids` per room, so removing one room from a template is a per-pair `dormant` flip and a renamed room is a visible new pair, which is the diff a migration step needs. The integers are **not persisted in `layout.state`** (the instance persists the `template_id` string, § 2); they exist so a rename or removal after `SHIPPED` is detected and migrated (ADR-0007 § 3.3), and so later blocks can reference a room by integer if they must.
191	
192	**The three hashes (the shape of ADR-LAY-06).** ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids an owner-written `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` byte string, and § 4.6 already defines the template hashes as `Hash64.of_value` of a post-cast sub-payload "whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's". 193	
194	| Hash | Payload (keys sorted by the encoder, so order in source is irrelevant; every family is one flat `PackedInt32Array` in the field order of its LY-4 row, strings replaced by template-local indices, variable-length members as a CSR `*_off` array plus a data array) | Changes when |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `geometry_hash` | `size_tiles`; `rooms` (origin, flags, tile runs); `wall_runs` (orientation, start, length, kind, flanking rooms, `face_h_px`, `face_variant`); the compiled `rects` (stride 7: `x0, y0, x1, y1, flags, owner_kind, owner_ref`, in `idx` order, leaf and variant slots at their closed or full extent); `doors`; `sockets` with their `lanes`; `hardpoints`; `plate_positions`; `loose_slots`; `story_slots`; `anchors` (polyline CSR); `fixture_anchors`; `instrument_placements` (geometry fields only) | anything that decides where a rectangle, tile, socket, door or anchor is |
197	| `visual_hash` | `dialect`; kit-piece ids and layers; art references; labels; advisory hints (`socket_tag`); flags no query reads | only presentation changes |
198	| `structure_hash` | the **ordered** key sequences: `room_key[]`, `socket_key[]`, `door_key[]`, `hp_key[]`, `node_ref[]`, `edge_ref[]`, `anchor_key[]`, `slot_id[]`; each room's sorted tile list | any reorder, add, remove or rename of an identity-bearing element, or any tile-set change |

203	
204	### 5. Rectangles, units and frames: the record, the flags and the reserved `idx` space
205	
206	ADR-0014 owns the broadphase, `QueryBuffer`, `OccluderSource` and the query signatures. This ADR owns **what a rectangle is, how it is keyed and which ones can exist**.
207	
208	- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`). The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
209	- **Units and frames.** The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` is the floor tile and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` the wall depth. There is no world frame in Layout. Reads answer **section-local** except those that answer for one body (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`), which answer in the **body frame** = section-local + `offset_px(section_id)` (LY-3 c).
210	- **Transforms are integer translation only.** No rotation, no mirror, no zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (LY-3 d, e). Every px-to-tile or px-to-cell conversion is **floor** division through `IntMath.floor_div` (body-frame coordinates may be negative after a detach re-base); the bare `/` and `%` operators appear nowhere in `src/sim/layout/` (ADR-0010 `SIM-05`).
211	- **The `idx` space is compiled once per template and never changes** (D.9): static rects sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` are `0 .. N_static - 1`; one reserved leaf slot per door follows in door declaration order; two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per **hatched** socket follow, `idx = N_static + N_doors + 2h + v`. The key `(section_id, idx)` is therefore stable across attach, detach, restore and animation: a state change only switches slots between active and inactive; an inactive or zero-length slot is omitted from results and keeps its `idx` (TR-section-020's "renumbers nothing" half).
212	- **Rect keys.** `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` with the stride `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, a power of two) and `idx < stride`; the key reaches `2^32 - 1`, so every key column is `PackedInt64Array` (ADR-0014 owns the buffer). Boot refuses a template whose `N_static + N_doors + 2 N_hatched` exceeds the stride (`RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`).
213	- **The compiled table is catalog data.** `SectionTemplate` exposes rect `idx`-indexed accessors (`rect_count()`, `rect_x0(i)`, `rect_y0(i)`, `rect_x1(i)`, `rect_y1(i)`, `rect_flags(i)`, `rect_owner_kind(i)`, `rect_owner_ref(i)`), never a packed array (ADR-0007 § 1.5). The bulk read that builds a body's grid at build, attach, detach and restore is ADR-0014's; those events are cold, so accessor calls are acceptable there (V3 measures them).
214	- **Static footprint set versus query set.** `rects_in` returns `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects and `solid_in` returns `SOLID` rects in their *current leaf state*; the mating overlap test of § 6 uses the **static** set with all flags, so a door animating can never flip a verdict. Both sets are views of one rect set (Pillar 1: collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); neither is an engine collision shape, and the avatar has no physics body.
215	
216	### 6. Sockets, seams and the mating predicate
217	
218	- **A socket is a pre-declared attachment site** `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[], hatch | none}` in the template (LY-13). `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S. The four-facing footprint, LOW-end, PLATE/JAMB/LEAF table of LY-13 is normative and is not restated.
219	- **States (TR-section-018, TR-assembly-025).** `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut); `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` never return to `FREE` in MVP, which supports exactly one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. **A socket's state is written only inside LM2 and LM3.** There is no `install_cap_plate`, no `set_socket_state` and no setter on `LayoutState.sockets`; `socket_state` writes are private to `weld_math`/`detach_planner` helpers called by those two mutators, and a lint (`LAY-SOCKET-01`, tier E1, ADR-0010 § 6) rejects any other write to the `sockets` columns.
220	- **`can_attach` is a pure, first-failure-wins reason chain** (TR-section-019), cheap before expensive, in this fixed order: `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `SAME_BODY` being a hard reject and every weld merging two bodies is what makes the weld relation a **forest** and a cut always split a body into exactly two components.
221	- **`GEOM_OVERLAP`.** The test set is the static footprint of both bodies after the D.6 translation: every static rect with all flags, each PLATE slot at its full footprint, no leaf and no JAMB slot, plus the tile cells of every room (rect against tile and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell both fail); abutting is legal. It runs over each body's broadphase handle (ADR-0014) and is **memoised on `(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`**; uncached cost target <= 2 ms (TR-section-019), a pending-spike figure (V3). The memo is a small fixed-capacity ring in `LayoutDerived`, reset on restore.
222	- **Slot activation is a pure function** of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` evaluated by LM1 to LM4 and `post_restore` (the LY-15 matrix); no persisted field is needed because the mate's hatch is known from the two templates. A hatched socket whose mate is bare is `hatch_one_sided`: legal, behaves bulkhead-only, its PLATE stays on while `WELDED`.
223	- **The `can_attach` preview needs more than a reason**, and a Class A check returns a bare `StringName` (ADR-0003 § 5). So the payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is its own pure read, `preview_attach(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: AttachPreview) -> void`, and `can_attach(...)` is `preview_attach` followed by returning `out.reason` (`&""` = OK). One implementation, two shapes.
224	- **`socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: WeldPlan)`** is a pure read that fills the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (one lane pair per lane in `(loop, lane_index)` order, one opening per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`). The field layout of `WeldPlan` follows ADR-0011's `JoinPlan`; Layout fills it, Assembly adds `q`, the Graph's `can_join` validates, and both verdicts must pass before apply.
225	
226	### 7. Weld offsets, bodies and the detach re-base
227	
228	**Bodies.** `bodies[]` is Layout's: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state}`. **Every built section starts on its own new body at offset (0, 0), and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (LY-25): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the forest property holds by construction. A body's frame origin is the origin of its `origin_section_id`.
229	
230	**Weld offset (D.6, TR-section-021).** `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b`, where `a` is the **survivor-side** socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned **by body, never by argument order**: the body with the **lower `body_id`** survives (the older body; the home ship in the MVP). `attach_section` re-labels the two arguments internally, so `attach_section(x, y, ...)` and `attach_section(y, x, ...)` produce the same survivor, the same `offset_b`, the same `frame_shift_px`, and a **byte-identical** `layout.state`: the `welds[]` row always records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` (canonicalisation). `weld_math.gd` is a pure module of integer helpers (`survivor_of`, `offset_b`, `frame_shift`) with no state, which `weld_offset(...)` (the pure read), `can_attach` and LM2 all call, so prediction and apply cannot drift.
231	
232	**24-grid closure.** `pos_a`, `pos_b` and `offset_a` lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` is a boot invariant, § 4), and `offset_a` does by induction from (0, 0), so `offset_b` does; an off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is therefore a **defect**, not a reason code: `apply` raises `LAYOUT_OFFSET_OFF_GRID` (domain 4) and returns its negative.
233	
234	**LM2 effects, in order** (all inside the caller's single P2 apply, after the Graph's `weld_join`): append the `welds[]` row (`ACTIVE`); upsert both socket rows to `WELDED(seam_id)` keeping ascending order; shift every section of the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px = offset_b - offset_b_old` and move it to the survivor `body_id`; mark the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switch the PLATE/JAMB/LEAF slots of both sockets (§ 6); seed each newly active LEAF **closed** with its last-projected cache (§ 8); rebuild the affected broadphase handles (ADR-0014); bump `static_version` and `version` of **every section whose socket state changed (including the host section that does not move) and every moved section**; stamp `changed_region` (REGION for the two socket-host sections, FRAME for the other moved sections); cache the mated hatch's opening ids from `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]` into `opening_leaves`; mark `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>` and `SEC/<id>` for each affected section (5 keys for the MVP weld of two single-section bodies). The returned `AttachResult` carries `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`; `body_of` of every moved section is the survivor in the same apply and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick.
235	
236	**LM3 and the detach re-base (D.12).** After the Graph's `cut_detach`, LM3 marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` (keeping `seam_id`); then **enumerates the connected components of the `ACTIVE` weld forest minus the cut seam, in ascending `section_id`**. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other receives a new `body_id` from `next_body_id`, its `origin_section_id` is `m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component, and its offsets are re-based by `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` (`offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) - frame_shift`). The traversal uses preallocated `PackedInt32Array` stack and visited columns in `LayoutDerived`, bounded by `MAX_SECTIONS`, so no container is built in the apply. `DetachPlanner.plan(...)` is the single implementation behind both `detach_preview(seam_id)` and LM3, so the preview and the apply cannot drift (Assembly's `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`). A cut that does not yield exactly two components is a defect (`LAYOUT_COMPONENT_COUNT`), unreachable by the forest argument. The `DetachResult` is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` the cut seam's two hatch rectangles in the pre-cut body frame, **computed before the sockets change**, exactly equal to `detach_preview(seam_id).rects`. Layout performs **no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`): the CHANNEL path is vetoed by Assembly's completion validate, and Body's `rebase_on_detach` is the net behind it (LY-17, BDY-24 iii).
237	
238	**Why not argument order or "the larger body".** Argument order makes the dissolved body depend on a caller's mixup (the home ship could dissolve) and makes the block bytes differ between two equal worlds, which breaks AC-172 (equal blocks by different histories hash equal). "Larger body survives" would make survival depend on a count that changes with every weld. The lower `body_id` is a persisted, immutable, total order.
239	
240	### 8. The door leaf, the `layout.doors` hook and the Graph port
241	
242	**One rectangle per leaf.** A door or hatch has one leaf rect. With `width_px` (the 96-px door cell), the Graph opening's `area` clamped to `[0, area_max]` and `area_max > 0`: `gap = floor_div(width_px * area, area_max)`, `leaf_w = width_px - gap`, and the rect is anchored to the hinge side with depth `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (D.5; hinge LOW for every socket hatch so both leaves of a mated hatch retract the same way). `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect and keeps its `idx`. A mated hatch is two leaves (one per section) driven by one `area`.
243	
244	**The port.** Layout reads and calls the Graph only through `LayoutGraphPort` (`src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd`, `@abstract`, ADR-0010 § 3), implemented by the Graph's facade and injected into `setup()`:
245	
246	```gdscript
247	@abstract class_name LayoutGraphPort extends RefCounted
248	@abstract func check_instantiate(views: SimViews, template_id: String) -> StringName   # Graph CAPACITY pre-check for can_build
249	@abstract func instantiate_section(scope: WriteScope, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int, out: SectionBases) -> int
250	@abstract func opening_into(edge_id: int, out: OpeningRead) -> bool   # false = unknown edge; fills area, area_max, door_state
251	@abstract func seam_openings_into(seam_id: int, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool   # opening_ids[] in socket_plan.openings order
252	@abstract func section_counts_into(section_id: int, out: SectionCounts) -> bool   # nodes, edges, compartments, next_section_id (verification only)
253	```
254	
255	The 4.7 typed-return rule applies to any override of a typed-return abstract method, so each implementation returns explicitly on every path (a stub that omits a return is a parse error or a defect found by V-lint). The reads are allocation-free (caller-owned `out`), valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes.
256	
257	**The hook (TR-section-012).** `layout.doors`: `hook_id &"layout.doors"`, owner Layout, `divisor 1`, `offset 0`, `after []`, running in P3. Body's `body.integrate` is registered `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` (BDY-8), which orders the Emitter after it transitively, so every P3 reader sees same-tick leaves. The hook loops over the `LayoutDerived` leaf cache, a dense list of at most `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` slots in ascending `(section_id, door_index)` (deterministic bump order):
258	
259	1. `graph.opening_into(edge, op)`. If it returns false (unknown opening) the leaf stays at its last projected value (closed at the template default), `area` is never invented, `leaf_version` is not bumped, and the diagnostic `opening_unknown` is raised **once per edge** (a bit in the slot's flags, cleared when the read succeeds again) (TR-section-035). A `area_max <= 0` read is treated the same way and counted `opening_invalid`.
260	2. `area` is clamped to `[0, area_max]`; a value above `area_max` raises the diagnostic `area_clamped` and uses `area_max` (TR-section-035).
261	3. `leaf_w` is computed (integer, `IntMath.floor_div`), compared with the slot's last-projected value, and if different the leaf rect is recomputed and the slot's section is flagged.
262	4. After the loop, for each flagged section in ascending id: `leaf_version += 1`, `version += 1`, never `static_version`; `changed_region` is stamped REGION(union of the old and new leaf rectangles). **At most one bump per section per tick** (TR-section-042).
263	5. If any section was flagged, the hook opens `layout.state` once (`scope.open_for`) and marks one **`LEAF/<section_id>`** key per flagged section.
264	
265	**Why the hook marks a key, and why a new kind.** `layout.doors` changes only derived caches, yet the PROJECTOR must redraw a leaf whose rect changed and the door leaf sprite extent must equal the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013). ADR-0009 presenters draw from dirty batches; polling every section's counter every frame would add a read per frame for an event that happens a few times per play. Marking is legal (ADR-0004 § 7: a key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation; the HOOK scope may open any block). Its cost is that a granted `open_for` advances `touch_serial`, invalidating the block hash cache (ADR-0005 § 5.2) on those ticks; under the binary door model that is a few ticks per play, and the re-encode is bounded by the block size (tens of KB). LY-32's closed list is SEC, BODY, SEAM; a leaf change under `SEC/<id>` would also wake Failure & Trail's anchor rebuild and Lighting's static rebuild on every door toggle, so the key family **`LEAF` (kind 4)** is added to Layout's own key space (ADR-0004 § 3 leaves unnumbered families to the owner). Subscribers that care (the PROJECTOR, Lighting's dynamic leaf patch) test `batch.has(key)`; the rest ignore it.
266	
267	**The correctness condition.** Every `area` write of a template door or mated hatch lands in **P2** by command (a SYSTEM-origin `set_opening` re-submitted each tick by Interaction's `attempts[]` for a `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry); no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state` of such an opening (the Graph's virtual breach and seam-weep openings have no leaf and are neither read nor projected). Layout stores, mirrors and writes neither value (TR-section-013); `layout_hash` does not cover door state. This is a cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011/0012/0020 and a test (AC "closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the same tick its state changes").
268	
269	**Seeding.** LM1 reads the just-created openings through the port and derives each leaf immediately (the Graph holds authored initial areas), so there is no tick in which a built door is wrong. **LM2 does not read the Graph's `area`:** it initialises each newly active LEAF **closed** (`leaf_w = width_px`) and seeds the last-projected cache with that value in the same apply, because `weld_join` starts the new opening at `area` 0; reads between the P2 apply and the first P3 hook therefore see a solid span, raise no `stale_leaf`, and the hook bumps `leaf_version` only if its `area` read differs (TR-section-034). `post_restore` derives all leaves in one `derive_doors` pass (§ 10).

I'm now spotting a cross-ADR conflict: ADR-0011 restricts GraphCaches writes to graph_derived.gd only, but ADR-0012 describes caches being updated by mutators and multiple phases at mark time, not just the derived-state file. This means ADR-0011 needs to widen its writer set to resolve the inconsistency.

Also noticing GraphScratch is supposed to be written exclusively by graph_propagate.gd, yet its sizing call in GraphCaches occurs within structural mutators and post_restore paths — that's effectively a mutating call from outside the declared writer, so the writer sets need revising there too. There's also a cross-ADR inconsistency between how ADR-0016 and ADR-0011 derive step_no (hdr vs clock) that seems like a low-priority issue owned by ADR-0016, so I want to check that line directly.

content.thinking:
ADR-0017 ties the fault glow to last_step_no, confirming it depends on failure-hook semantics and that T2 blocking holds. Checking ADR-0012, the descriptor store window is re-derived at the restore tick, and since the Emitter only reconciles on a newly completed step, it correctly pulls from the store after phase 11 — consistent with expectations.

Cross-checking ADR-0011's GraphView getters against ADR-0017's needs (node_state, served_pm, run_pm, section_of, section_dormant, last_step_no) — all present. For ADR-0028, computing per-section means from per-compartment nodes_in requires iterating compartments filtered by section, which is workable but clunky; I also notice there's no direct node_subtype(id) getter to identify lamp fixtures, just node_kind, so I should flag adding a load_subtype(id) getter as a minor gap. ADR-0034 has no issues, and ADR-0026 is fine with M19/M1 in INIT scope. Now I'm moving to ADR-0012's GraphTuning offsets and boot assertions.

The MAX_GRAPH_EDGES bound needs updating from 2^20 to 2^18 in a couple spots — minor fix. My overall verdict lands on CONCERNS rather than REJECT since the decision itself is sound, but there are real blocking findings: the served_pm classification contradicts ADR-0012's restore-equivalence finding and ADR-0017 depends on it; last_step_no semantics need resolution since FAULT_GLOW and FT-15 depend on them; and the writer-file sets contradict ADR-0012's propagate/ directory structure in a way that would trip the OWN-01 lint config, making it a blocking registry-pattern issue. I'm now moving into a fourth blocking point about layering.

T4 is about a missing LayoutGraphPort surface — functions like check_instantiate, instantiate_section, opening_into, seam_openings_into, and section_counts_into — plus confusion over which caller (Layout LM1 vs Web Map) should use it; this blocks the Layout epic's Wave-A port since ADR-0013 R7 depends on it. Then T5 raises the hook cursor restore check and HOOK_CURSOR fault code 25, which ADR-0012 assigns to a verifier ADR-0016 doesn't actually have — I'm weighing whether this is truly blocking, since the cursor check matters for catching corrupt saves where the cursor doesn't match the step, though a legitimate restore between hooks could show differing cursors without being a fault.

I'm concluding that without this check, an inconsistent save would surface as a mid-play HOOK_CURSOR fault instead of a clean restore failure, so I'll mark it medium, non-blocking but strongly recommended, bundled with a trivial fault-table append for code 25. T6 covers a Jacobi next-columns-vs-accumulators terminology mismatch across sections — low-medium, non-blocking, possibly mergeable with T3 but I'll keep it separate. T7 flags an undefined stale-id read sentinel per getter, medium non-blocking. T8 raises snapshot size headroom concerns since the fixture is at-weld and doesn't cover worst-case lifetime state, medium non-blocking. T9 is starting to note drift in the Key Interfaces section, where the set_valve snippet omits the topology rebuild/TOPO key and the setup signature is missing WorkCounter.

I'm continuing through more drift and consistency checks: the setup signature clock mismatch, header dictionary vs member naming, and a hardcoded "divisor 6" that should probably be tunable (low priority). T10 questions whether descriptor store ordering correctly relies on SUBJECT_KIND ordinal matching visit order, with an undefined OPENING anchor and possible double-processing of OPENING edges — low-medium. T11 notes default_state should apply a snapshot-shaped payload through its own restore mechanism rather than just describing state — low priority. T12 covers right-sizing observations: the ADR is appropriately sized, the ids.lock.json ledger approach is acceptable even though ADR-0007 avoided it, and FailureFilter.loaded_only appears dead but is kept intentionally for stability — I'll note this as low, non-blocking. T13 is starting to address an RNG id field update tied to a 2^18 range.

Then I move to the exogenous clear rule closing open question 3, the ONSET_UNKEYED reasoning, new GraphCaches/GraphDiag members, and the FailureFilter.loaded_only flag always being true — all low, non-blocking bookkeeping fixes aligned with ADR-0012. T14 checks that spike gating is honestly documented (S0-a, S1, S3, LINT-SPIKE-1 all named with status), noting the 32KB fixture is synthetic but value-independent, so no real finding there. I also flag a low-priority stock_pm window issue where stock can exceed the 1000 cap for up to five ticks before the first power hook.

Finally I start cataloguing cross-ADR ownership items: C1 covers n_served/n_draw ownership under ADR-0011 across multiple ADRs, C2 assigns last_step_no semantics to ADR-0012 with an amendment in ADR-0011 §2.3, and C3 begins addressing writer set ownership under ADR-0011.

findings.text: Contradiction with ADR-0012 § 11 (and ADR-0017 D14.4) on the persisted/derived split. ADR-0011 § 6.1, § 7.4 (3) and Alternative 7 class `served_pm` as DERIVED and reject persisting it on read-cost grounds. ADR-0012 § 11 shows that a restore landing between the power hook (6n+0) and the atmo or failure hook (6n+2, 6n+4) cannot rebuild `served`, `draw` or the cable net load from the post-phase state: batteries have been debited, the thermostat duty has moved, a cable may have failed, or M10 has changed `req`. The restored run would then diverge in `hp` by one step's damage. Alternative 7 never addresses this restore-equivalence argument. As written, the control manifest would extract 'never persist served_pm', which is the opposite of what ADR-0012 phase 2 writes and ADR-0012's Implementation Guidelines require ('must never read served_pm from a cache').
findings.amendment: Adopt ADR-0012's request. (a) In § 3.2, add node columns `n_served` (i32 permille) and `n_draw` (i32, dJ per step), with canonical zero on every node that is not a power consumer and range specs in `GraphSchema`. (b) In § 3.4, define `e0` of a CABLE edge as its net load in W, with a stated sign convention and min/max. (c) In § 6.1, move `served_pm` from DERIVED to PERSISTED and add a row 'hook products: n_served, n_draw, CABLE e0, written by phase 2 only'. (d) Rewrite § 7.4 (3) to say post_restore re-derives `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm` and trend but never `served`. (e) Rewrite Alternative 7 so it rejects persisting only the intensive atmosphere values and cites ADR-0012 § 11 for the hook products. (f) Update § 3.11, Risks 1, the performance_budgets registry candidate and the Validation size line to about 30.5 KB with about 4.6 percent headroom. (g) Remove `served_pm` from the `derived_members.json` description. (h) Add GDD sync items for LS-21, LS-4 and TR-lsg-004 wording. If you refuse, say so explicitly and list ADR-0012's three boundary divergences (battery final step, thermostat flip, cable failure between hooks) as accepted known divergences.

findings.text: `hdr.last_step_no` semantics conflict. § 2.3 defines it as 'the last step whose power hook completed' and says the step and `last_step_no` 'differ only between a tick and its first hook'. ADR-0012 § 1 (citing GDD LS-8) defines it as the last complete step, written by the failure hook at its end. ADR-0017's FAULT_GLOW reconcile (D6.4, 'reconcile only when GraphView.last_step_no() != hdr.fault_step_seen') and Failure & Trail's FT-15 poll depend on the failure-hook meaning: under ADR-0011's wording they would reconcile against a descriptor store that phase 11 has not yet rebuilt.
findings.amendment: Rewrite the last sentence of § 2.3: '`hdr.last_step_no` is the last step whose failure hook (phase 11) completed (LS-8, ADR-0012 § 1); it trails `step_no()` by up to one step, and equals it only from the end of the failure hook until the next power-hook tick.' Make § 3.8's hdr list and the `GraphView.last_step_no()` doc comment say the same.

findings.text: The writer-file sets in § 1 (table), § 12.1, Implementation Guidelines and the registry candidate `graph_field_write_outside_writer_files` conflict with ADR-0012's design, so the proposed OWN-01 configuration would flag the code ADR-0012 specifies. (1) ADR-0012 puts the phases in a `src/sim/graph/propagate/` directory (twelve phase files plus a dispatcher), not the single file `graph_propagate.gd`. (2) `GraphCaches` is said to be written by `graph_derived.gd` only, but in ADR-0012: phase 7 writes the `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm` and trend caches; phase 11 writes the descriptor store and `caches.alarm_sections`; and every marker, including mutators in `graph_mutators.gd`, updates the last-emitted buckets ('updated at every mark, whoever marked it'). (3) `GraphScratch` is said to be written by the propagate file only, yet ADR-0012 sizes it through `GraphCaches.size_scratch()` from structural mutators and `post_restore`, and a `resize` is a mutating call under § 12.1.
findings.amendment: Rewrite § 12.1 and the § 1 table as one writer matrix per class. GraphState: `propagate/**`, `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_restore.gd`. GraphCaches: `graph_derived.gd` plus either (i) `propagate/**` and `graph_mutators.gd` for the named members (intensive values, descriptor store, alarm list, last-emitted buckets), or (ii) a rule that phases and mutators write those members only by calling `GraphDerived` functions. State which option you choose. GraphScratch: `propagate/**` for contents, `graph_derived.gd` for sizing. Update the `field_writers.json` schema in Foundation Ask 1 to accept directory globs (merging ADR-0012 Foundation Ask 1), and update the forbidden_patterns registry candidate and the Implementation Guidelines to match.

findings.text: The Graph side of ADR-0013's `LayoutGraphPort` is missing. ADR-0013 § 8 declares five abstract methods that 'the Graph's facade' implements: `check_instantiate(views, template_id: String) -> StringName`, `instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out: SectionBases) -> int`, `opening_into(edge_id, out: OpeningRead) -> bool`, `seam_openings_into(seam_id, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool` and `section_counts_into(section_id, out: SectionCounts) -> bool`. ADR-0013 R7 says its §§ 3, 8 and 10 change if ADR-0011 does not supply them. ADR-0011 names none of the four reads and calls M1's out object `InstantiateResult`, where ADR-0013 calls it `SectionBases`. ADR-0011 § 1 and the ADR-0012 assumption also say Web Map's `init_world` calls M1 directly, but ADR-0013 routes it as Web Map → LM1 → port.instantiate_section, so that Layout allocates `section_id` first. A Layout or Graph story written today would pick one of two incompatible call chains.
findings.amendment: Add a § 9.5 'Layout port' and a Key Interfaces snippet. It should declare the Graph facade class (for example `GraphLayoutPort extends LayoutGraphPort` in `src/sim/graph/ports/`, injected by the composition root), implementing all five methods: allocation-free, caller-owned outs, valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes. `opening_into` derives `door_state` from `area`. `seam_openings_into` returns `opening_ids` in `socket_plan.openings` order and stays valid after restore. `section_counts_into` reads persisted columns only (Tier S). `check_instantiate` is the pure CAPACITY and LS-18 reason check that ADR-0012 calls `check_instantiate_section`. Unify the out type name (one of `InstantiateResult` or `SectionBases`) in § 11 and the registry candidate. Reword § 1's 'init_world, binding_source' row and § 4.4: M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through the port, and LM1's only caller is Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope.

findings.text: A restore check for the hook cursors is missing and is now owned by nobody. ADR-0012 § 1 adds the runtime guard `HOOK_CURSOR` (local code 25) and asks ADR-0016 to verify `last_step_power/atmo/failure` against the restored clock. ADR-0016 has no cursor verifier (grep finds none), and its V3 row only cites ADR-0011 § 7.2's twelve steps. § 7.2's static [min, max] specs cannot classify a save whose `last_step_X` exceeds the step implied by `T`. Such a save restores successfully, and the first hook then raises HOOK_CURSOR mid-play, which turns a classifiable corrupt input into an in-play FAULTED.
findings.amendment: In one append-only batch, append local code 25 `HOOK_CURSOR` (ADR-0012's runtime guard) and code 26 `RESTORE_CURSOR` to § 8.1, then add a § 7.2 step after step 7. The step checks each `last_step_X` against the installed clock (ADR-0016 R2 installs it before R3): it must equal the step of the last tick at or before T on which hook X was due, under ADR-0012's step-0 convention, and `last_step_no == last_step_failure`. The reason is `RESTORE_CURSOR(hook, expected, got)`. Update the 1,000-mutation fuzz reason table, and record in Related that ADR-0016 V3 now covers it via § 7.2.

findings.text: Stale-id reads are underspecified. § 4.1 (5) says a read of a stale or tombstoned id 'returns the neutral value', but defines it per getter nowhere. ADR-0017 assumes 'a not-live sentinel without faulting'. For `node_state(id)` the natural neutral 0 is `NODE_STATE` OK, the opposite of not-live: an Emitter or Interaction reader would treat a tombstoned or never-allocated node as healthy. The same ambiguity affects `edge_state`, `section_of` (0 is EXTERIOR's section) and `compartment_*`.
findings.amendment: Add a sentinel column to the § 9.1 hot-path list. Suggested values: `node_state`/`edge_state` return -1 (NOT_LIVE, outside the `NODE_STATE` domain); `node_kind` -1; `section_of` -1; `served_pm`/`run_pm`/`stock_pm`/`node_hp` 0; `compartment_*` -1 for a cid with no `comps` row. Alternatively, add `node_live(id)`/`edge_live(id) -> bool` and require readers to guard with it. Add a test that every hot getter answers its documented sentinel for id -1, an id at or above the counter, and a tombstone.

findings.text: The purity statement in § 9.1 contradicts itself and ADR-0012 § 4. It says no getter 'writes any member of any of the four classes', then says the view 'may call `ensure_derived()`'. In ADR-0012 that call rebuilds `GraphCaches` and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds` when it finds `topo_dirty` set. The property actually guaranteed is 'writes no persisted column, emits no key, draws no RNG; the hash is unchanged'.
findings.amendment: Reword § 9.1 purity: 'No getter writes any GraphState column, marks a dirty key or draws RNG, so `state_hash` is unchanged. The one permitted side effect is the defect-only `ensure_derived()` guard (ADR-0012 § 4), which writes GraphCaches and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds`, asserted zero in every test.' Align the Implementation Guidelines bullet 'no write to any member'.

findings.text: The snapshot-size evidence covers the at-weld roster only. The 29.7 KB fixture (about 30.5 KB after T1, 4.6 percent headroom) is the loaded set at the weld. Rows are never removed: tombstones persist in the payload, RAGGED cuts append stub HULL_SEGMENT rows, cut seams keep their lists, and `defs` never shrinks. ADR-0013 § 6 permits one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. The lifetime-worst reachable state (every socket cycled once with RAGGED cuts, every queue at its bound, all defs interned) is therefore larger than the measured fixture, and no Validation item measures it. Separately, § 3.11's '32 KB is reached near 114 nodes' is at most 9 nodes away.
findings.amendment: Add a 'lifetime-worst' fixture to Validation and § 3.11: every socket welded and cut RAGGED once (ADR-0013 § 6 bound), queues at bound, maximal defs. Either show it fits under 32 KB or pre-commit lever 1 (the fluid-stamp side table) now, with the tradeoff stated. Cite ADR-0013's one-cycle-per-socket rule as the bound that makes tombstone growth finite at MVP.

findings.text: `GraphView`, the contract eight consumers code against, exists only as a prose list in § 9.1, with no Key Interfaces skeleton. Some reads that consumers need are absent from that list: a LOAD subtype getter for ADR-0028's fixture filter (TR-light-034 requires excluding non-Graph or self-powered fixtures and identifying lamp LOADs), a per-section compartment enumeration (TR-light-034's mean is per section, so a consumer must currently scan all compartments through `cid_at` and filter by `section_of`), and the descriptor-row getters of § 9.4, named only with ellipses.
findings.amendment: Add a `graph_view.gd` Key Interfaces skeleton with typed signatures and sentinel doc comments (T6) for every hot getter, including `load_subtype(id) -> int`, `compartments_in_section(section_id, out: PackedInt32Array) -> int` (ascending) and the full `desc_*` getter list. Tag each `## @hot` for the HOT-01 list.

findings.text: § 9.3 claims the descriptor store is sorted by construction, but the claim rests on unstated preconditions. The key is `(subject_kind << 40) | (subject_id << 8) | mode`, and the visit order is NODE, EDGE, COMPARTMENT, SEAM, OPENING. Strict ascent therefore requires the `GraphIds.SUBJECT_KIND` ordinals to be NODE < EDGE < COMPARTMENT < SEAM < OPENING, which is never pinned, and `ids.lock.json` would freeze whatever is written first. It also requires that OPENING edges are excluded from the EDGE pass, or that both passes cannot produce the same key, which is also unstated. The OPENING subject's anchor is undefined (the anchor bullet covers NODE, EDGE, COMPARTMENT and SEAM only).
findings.amendment: In § 4.7 or § 9.3, fix `SUBJECT_KIND` ordinals to the visit order (for example NODE 1, EDGE 2, COMPARTMENT 3, SEAM 4, OPENING 5). State that OPENING-kind edges are visited only in the OPENING pass. Define the OPENING anchor (for example `anchor_a` = edge id, `anchor_b` = -1).

findings.text: The Key Interfaces and internal text have drifted from each other and from ADR-0012. (a) The header's in-memory form is ambiguous: § 3.8 and the Implementation Guidelines say GraphState holds 'a Dictionary of int', while Key Interfaces declares `_h_*: int` members. The § 6.3 reflection allowlist differs between the two. (b) The `set_valve` snippet marks only EDGE and does not rebuild, but ADR-0012 § 6 says M8 changes connectivity, rebuilds and marks TOPO. Implementers copy snippets. (c) `GraphModule.setup` lacks ADR-0012's `work: WorkCounter`, the `graph.fail` stream registration and the ClockView source. (d) § 1 hard-codes 'divisor 6, offsets 0, 2, 4', where ADR-0012 makes both `GraphTuning` data. (e) `GraphFault.raise_ctx` mutates the caller's `detail` Dictionary.
findings.amendment: (a) Choose `_h_*` int members and state that the snapshot builds the hdr Dictionary. (b) Make the `set_valve` excerpt set `topo_dirty`, call `GraphDerived.ensure_derived`, and mark `EDGE` and `TOPO`, or cut it to a mutator that does not change connectivity (for example M10). (c) Adopt ADR-0012's `setup` signature. (d) Say 'divisor `tuning.graph_step_ticks`, offsets `tuning.hook_offset_*`'. (e) Copy `detail` before adding `subject`, or document the ownership transfer.

findings.text: Sibling ADRs have closed several items that ADR-0011 still carries open, and the Graph-side additions they ask for have not been adopted. Open Question 2 is closed by ADR-0016 (phase 0). Open Question 3 is closed by ADR-0012 § 7 (the EXOGENOUS clear rule). Open Question 8 and Risk 7 are closed by ADR-0012 § 8.2 (2-bit kind, 18-bit id), so § 4.1 (4) and § 8.4's '2^20 RNG subject field' becomes 2^18. Not yet adopted: `ONSET_UNKEYED` in the M1 check; `GraphIds.ALARM_CAPABLE_MASK`; the `GraphTuning` hook offsets, `load_queue_max`, `w_min_steps` and burst fields; the `GraphCaches` members `active_*`, `store_slots`, `machine_slots`, `exchange_links`, the POWER island list and `alarm_sections`; the `GraphDiag` counters `late_rebuilds`, `queue_dropped` and `footprints_clamped`; and the note that `FailureFilter.loaded_only` is always satisfied because the store holds loaded sections only.
findings.amendment: Mark Open Questions 2, 3 and 8 and Risk 7 as resolved, with pointers to the closing ADRs. Change 2^20 to 2^18 in § 4.1 (4) and § 8.4. Add a short 'Adopted from ADR-0012' list covering the GraphIds, GraphTuning, GraphCaches and GraphDiag additions, and require that `derived_members.json` includes them. Document `loaded_only` as retained for type stability and always true.

findings.text: Three smaller gaps. (a) § 4.6 describes the EMPTY state but not the ADR-0016 § 3.3 mechanism: `default_state(ctx)` must `ctx.put` a snapshot-shaped payload that the Graph's own `restore` accepts, and KRN-RST-07 tests that path. (b) After a restore of a store above a lowered `stock_cap`, readers and M16 `withdraw_store` see over-cap stock, and `stock_pm` can exceed 1000, for up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks until the phase-0 reconcile; for a dormant section the window lasts until the section loads. Neither window is stated. (c) `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` (step 11) does not mention resolution through the ADR-0007 alias path, which ADR-0016 assumes. ADR-0007 defers aliases to a pre-SHIPPED story.
findings.amendment: (a) Add to § 4.6: '`default_state` builds this state as a payload with `GraphSchema` keys, `ctx.put`s it, and the kernel applies it through `GraphRestore.restore` (ADR-0016 § 3.3); the payload passes all § 7.2 steps.' (b) State in § 7.3 that `stock_pm` clamps to 1000 and that M16 may withdraw over-cap stock in the window, or forbid that, and give the dormant-section case. (c) Add to step 11: 'after `resolve_alias` once ADR-0007's alias story lands; the stored def string is not rewritten'.

findings.text: Gate items that pass: the problem statement and rationale are clear; alternatives 1 to 9 are genuinely considered; the Consequences section is honest (overlay readability, the indirection cost, no compaction, the 12x division cost); the engine is stamped as Godot 4.7.2 with Knowledge Risk MEDIUM; post-cutoff APIs (`@abstract` 4.5, typed Dictionary 4.4, both 4.7 GDScript rows) are flagged and probed on the editor binary, with the release-export gaps (S0-a/S0-b, S1, S3, LINT-SPIKE-1) named rather than claimed. TR traceability is complete: every row planned for ADR-0011 in requirements-traceability.md (TR-lsg-001..006, 018, 019, 024, 038; itemdb-014, 016, 031, 033, 040; instr-027; boarding-041; light-034; and the residuals of lsg-020, 022, 023, 030, 033 and itemdb-036) appears in a Decided-here or Owned-elsewhere table. The layout is right-sized for a determinism-critical solo MVP. The only addition beyond what Foundation required, `ids.lock.json` for persisted Graph enums, is a defensible zero-mechanism reuse of ADR-0007's ledger.
findings.amendment: None required. Optionally, state the right-sizing and spike-gating conclusion in the Review Log when the amendments land.

cross_adr.text: Persisted hook products. ADR-0012 § 11 requires `n_served`, `n_draw` and CABLE `e0` net load to be persisted for restore equivalence on any tick. ADR-0017 depends on `served_pm` being exact after restore. ADR-0011 currently classes `served_pm` as DERIVED and rejects persisting it (Alternative 7). The column decision is ADR-0011's.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 adopts the three columns per finding T1 and updates the size to about 30.5 KB. ADR-0012 § 11 and ADR-0017 then drop their conditional 'if ADR-0011 declines' fallback text.

cross_adr.text: `last_step_no` meaning. ADR-0012 § 1 owns the hook cursors and defines `last_step_no` as the step whose failure hook completed (LS-8). ADR-0017's FAULT_GLOW reconcile and FT-15 depend on that meaning. ADR-0011 § 2.3 says 'power hook'. ADR-0011 is the amender, not the owner.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 § 2.3, § 3.8 and the `GraphView.last_step_no()` comment adopt ADR-0012 § 1's definition verbatim (finding T2).

cross_adr.text: Graph writer-file matrix and the OWN-01 configuration. ADR-0011 § 12.1 names a single `graph_propagate.gd` and makes GraphCaches writable only by `graph_derived.gd`. ADR-0012 has a `propagate/` directory, writes caches in phases 7 and 11, updates last-emitted buckets from mutators, and sizes scratch from the derived file. ADR-0010 must accept directory globs in `field_writers.json`.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 publishes one per-class writer matrix (finding T3) and merges ADR-0012 Foundation Ask 1 (glob support) into its own Foundation Ask 1 to ADR-0010. ADR-0012's Key Interfaces comment then cites ADR-0011 § 12.1 instead of restating the set.

cross_adr.text: `LayoutGraphPort` and the M1 call chain. ADR-0013 § 8 defines the port: `check_instantiate`, `instantiate_section(..., out: SectionBases)`, `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`. It routes M1 as Web Map `init_world` → LM1 → port, so that Layout allocates `section_id` first. ADR-0011 implements none of the reads, names the out type `InstantiateResult`, and (with ADR-0012 § 6) says Web Map calls M1 directly. ADR-0013 owns the port definition; ADR-0011 is the implementer.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 adds the facade `extends LayoutGraphPort` with all five methods (finding T4) and adopts one out-type name; whichever name is chosen, ADR-0013 and ADR-0011 must match. ADR-0011 § 1 and ADR-0012 § 6 (M1 row and Rules) reword M1's caller as 'Layout LM1 through LayoutGraphPort, itself called only by Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope'. ADR-0013 § 3's table fixes two wording errors: there is no 'comp counter' (cid is the COMPARTMENT node id, from `next_node_id`), and opening ids are edge ids from `next_edge_id`, not from `next_seam_id`.

cross_adr.text: Hook-cursor restore verification. ADR-0012 assigns it to ADR-0016's verifier, but ADR-0016 has no cursor check; its V3 row delegates to ADR-0011 § 7.2. The Graph's fault table and restore precedence are ADR-0011's.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 appends `HOOK_CURSOR` (25) and `RESTORE_CURSOR` (26) and adds a § 7.2 step that checks each cursor against the clock installed at ADR-0016 R2 (finding T5). ADR-0012 § 1 changes its cross-ADR note from ADR-0016 to ADR-0011 § 7.2. ADR-0016's V3 text ('the ordered steps of ADR-0011 § 7.2') then covers it without change.

cross_adr.text: Stale-id read sentinel. ADR-0017 assumes `GraphView` getters return a not-live sentinel for an unknown or tombstoned id. ADR-0011 § 4.1 (5) says 'neutral value', which for `node_state` is 0 (OK).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 defines per-getter sentinels or `node_live`/`edge_live` guards (finding T6). ADR-0017 cites them by name.

cross_adr.text: Contents of GraphScratch. ADR-0012 § 3 replaces ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4)'s Jacobi `next` columns with delta accumulators (JAC discipline), so at MVP GraphScratch holds accumulators and traversal buffers only. ADR-0011 § 1, § 6.1 and § 6.2 still describe `next` columns.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0016's Tier S list cites the Graph 'step_no (from hdr)' for Suit V7 and Interaction V10 decoding. ADR-0011 § 2.3 defines `step_no()` as `floor_div(clock.tick(), GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`, which is valid once ADR-0016 R2 installs the clock. The hdr holds only cursors, which may trail by up to one step (T2), so 'from hdr' would give a different number.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0016 rewords the Tier S entry to 'GraphView.step_no() (derived from the installed kernel clock at R2, not from hdr)'. ADR-0011 needs no change beyond T2.

findings.text: Contradiction with ADR-0012 § 11 (and ADR-0017 D14.4) on the persisted/derived split. ADR-0011 § 6.1, § 7.4 (3) and Alternative 7 class `served_pm` as DERIVED and reject persisting it on read-cost grounds. ADR-0012 § 11 shows that a restore landing between the power hook (6n+0) and the atmo or failure hook (6n+2, 6n+4) cannot rebuild `served`, `draw` or the cable net load from the post-phase state: batteries have been debited, the thermostat duty has moved, a cable may have failed, or M10 has changed `req`. The restored run would then diverge in `hp` by one step's damage. Alternative 7 never addresses this restore-equivalence argument. As written, the control manifest would extract 'never persist served_pm', which is the opposite of what ADR-0012 phase 2 writes and ADR-0012's Implementation Guidelines require ('must never read served_pm from a cache').
findings.amendment: Adopt ADR-0012's request. (a) In § 3.2, add node columns `n_served` (i32 permille) and `n_draw` (i32, dJ per step), with canonical zero on every node that is not a power consumer and range specs in `GraphSchema`. (b) In § 3.4, define `e0` of a CABLE edge as its net load in W, with a stated sign convention and min/max. (c) In § 6.1, move `served_pm` from DERIVED to PERSISTED and add a row 'hook products: n_served, n_draw, CABLE e0, written by phase 2 only'. (d) Rewrite § 7.4 (3) to say post_restore re-derives `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm` and trend but never `served`. (e) Rewrite Alternative 7 so it rejects persisting only the intensive atmosphere values and cites ADR-0012 § 11 for the hook products. (f) Update § 3.11, Risks 1, the performance_budgets registry candidate and the Validation size line to about 30.5 KB with about 4.6 percent headroom. (g) Remove `served_pm` from the `derived_members.json` description. (h) Add GDD sync items for LS-21, LS-4 and TR-lsg-004 wording. If you refuse, say so explicitly and list ADR-0012's three boundary divergences (battery final step, thermostat flip, cable failure between hooks) as accepted known divergences.

findings.text: `hdr.last_step_no` semantics conflict. § 2.3 defines it as 'the last step whose power hook completed' and says the step and `last_step_no` 'differ only between a tick and its first hook'. ADR-0012 § 1 (citing GDD LS-8) defines it as the last complete step, written by the failure hook at its end. ADR-0017's FAULT_GLOW reconcile (D6.4, 'reconcile only when GraphView.last_step_no() != hdr.fault_step_seen') and Failure & Trail's FT-15 poll depend on the failure-hook meaning: under ADR-0011's wording they would reconcile against a descriptor store that phase 11 has not yet rebuilt.
findings.amendment: Rewrite the last sentence of § 2.3: '`hdr.last_step_no` is the last step whose failure hook (phase 11) completed (LS-8, ADR-0012 § 1); it trails `step_no()` by up to one step, and equals it only from the end of the failure hook until the next power-hook tick.' Make § 3.8's hdr list and the `GraphView.last_step_no()` doc comment say the same.

findings.text: The writer-file sets in § 1 (table), § 12.1, Implementation Guidelines and the registry candidate `graph_field_write_outside_writer_files` conflict with ADR-0012's design, so the proposed OWN-01 configuration would flag the code ADR-0012 specifies. (1) ADR-0012 puts the phases in a `src/sim/graph/propagate/` directory (twelve phase files plus a dispatcher), not the single file `graph_propagate.gd`. (2) `GraphCaches` is said to be written by `graph_derived.gd` only, but in ADR-0012: phase 7 writes the `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm` and trend caches; phase 11 writes the descriptor store and `caches.alarm_sections`; and every marker, including mutators in `graph_mutators.gd`, updates the last-emitted buckets ('updated at every mark, whoever marked it'). (3) `GraphScratch` is said to be written by the propagate file only, yet ADR-0012 sizes it through `GraphCaches.size_scratch()` from structural mutators and `post_restore`, and a `resize` is a mutating call under § 12.1.
findings.amendment: Rewrite § 12.1 and the § 1 table as one writer matrix per class. GraphState: `propagate/**`, `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_restore.gd`. GraphCaches: `graph_derived.gd` plus either (i) `propagate/**` and `graph_mutators.gd` for the named members (intensive values, descriptor store, alarm list, last-emitted buckets), or (ii) a rule that phases and mutators write those members only by calling `GraphDerived` functions. State which option you choose. GraphScratch: `propagate/**` for contents, `graph_derived.gd` for sizing. Update the `field_writers.json` schema in Foundation Ask 1 to accept directory globs (merging ADR-0012 Foundation Ask 1), and update the forbidden_patterns registry candidate and the Implementation Guidelines to match.

findings.text: The Graph side of ADR-0013's `LayoutGraphPort` is missing. ADR-0013 § 8 declares five abstract methods that 'the Graph's facade' implements: `check_instantiate(views, template_id: String) -> StringName`, `instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out: SectionBases) -> int`, `opening_into(edge_id, out: OpeningRead) -> bool`, `seam_openings_into(seam_id, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool` and `section_counts_into(section_id, out: SectionCounts) -> bool`. ADR-0013 R7 says its §§ 3, 8 and 10 change if ADR-0011 does not supply them. ADR-0011 names none of the four reads and calls M1's out object `InstantiateResult`, where ADR-0013 calls it `SectionBases`. ADR-0011 § 1 and the ADR-0012 assumption also say Web Map's `init_world` calls M1 directly, but ADR-0013 routes it as Web Map → LM1 → port.instantiate_section, so that Layout allocates `section_id` first. A Layout or Graph story written today would pick one of two incompatible call chains.
findings.amendment: Add a § 9.5 'Layout port' and a Key Interfaces snippet. It should declare the Graph facade class (for example `GraphLayoutPort extends LayoutGraphPort` in `src/sim/graph/ports/`, injected by the composition root), implementing all five methods: allocation-free, caller-owned outs, valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes. `opening_into` derives `door_state` from `area`. `seam_openings_into` returns `opening_ids` in `socket_plan.openings` order and stays valid after restore. `section_counts_into` reads persisted columns only (Tier S). `check_instantiate` is the pure CAPACITY and LS-18 reason check that ADR-0012 calls `check_instantiate_section`. Unify the out type name (one of `InstantiateResult` or `SectionBases`) in § 11 and the registry candidate. Reword § 1's 'init_world, binding_source' row and § 4.4: M1's only caller is Layout LM1 through the port, and LM1's only caller is Web Map `init_world` in the INIT scope.

findings.text: A restore check for the hook cursors is missing and is now owned by nobody. ADR-0012 § 1 adds the runtime guard `HOOK_CURSOR` (local code 25) and asks ADR-0016 to verify `last_step_power/atmo/failure` against the restored clock. ADR-0016 has no cursor verifier (grep finds none), and its V3 row only cites ADR-0011 § 7.2's twelve steps. § 7.2's static [min, max] specs cannot classify a save whose `last_step_X` exceeds the step implied by `T`. Such a save restores successfully, and the first hook then raises HOOK_CURSOR mid-play, which turns a classifiable corrupt input into an in-play FAULTED.
findings.amendment: In one append-only batch, append local code 25 `HOOK_CURSOR` (ADR-0012's runtime guard) and code 26 `RESTORE_CURSOR` to § 8.1, then add a § 7.2 step after step 7. The step checks each `last_step_X` against the installed clock (ADR-0016 R2 installs it before R3): it must equal the step of the last tick at or before T on which hook X was due, under ADR-0012's step-0 convention, and `last_step_no == last_step_failure`. The reason is `RESTORE_CURSOR(hook, expected, got)`. Update the 1,000-mutation fuzz reason table, and record in Related that ADR-0016 V3 now covers it via § 7.2.

findings.text: Stale-id reads are underspecified. § 4.1 (5) says a read of a stale or tombstoned id 'returns the neutral value', but defines it per getter nowhere. ADR-0017 assumes 'a not-live sentinel without faulting'. For `node_state(id)` the natural neutral 0 is `NODE_STATE` OK, the opposite of not-live: an Emitter or Interaction reader would treat a tombstoned or never-allocated node as healthy. The same ambiguity affects `edge_state`, `section_of` (0 is EXTERIOR's section) and `compartment_*`.
findings.amendment: Add a sentinel column to the § 9.1 hot-path list. Suggested values: `node_state`/`edge_state` return -1 (NOT_LIVE, outside the `NODE_STATE` domain); `node_kind` -1; `section_of` -1; `served_pm`/`run_pm`/`stock_pm`/`node_hp` 0; `compartment_*` -1 for a cid with no `comps` row. Alternatively, add `node_live(id)`/`edge_live(id) -> bool` and require readers to guard with it. Add a test that every hot getter answers its documented sentinel for id -1, an id at or above the counter, and a tombstone.

findings.text: The purity statement in § 9.1 contradicts itself and ADR-0012 § 4. It says no getter 'writes any member of any of the four classes', then says the view 'may call `ensure_derived()`'. In ADR-0012 that call rebuilds `GraphCaches` and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds` when it finds `topo_dirty` set. The property actually guaranteed is 'writes no persisted column, emits no key, draws no RNG; the hash is unchanged'.
findings.amendment: Reword § 9.1 purity: 'No getter writes any GraphState column, marks a dirty key or draws RNG, so `state_hash` is unchanged. The one permitted side effect is the defect-only `ensure_derived()` guard (ADR-0012 § 4), which writes GraphCaches and increments `GraphDiag.late_rebuilds`, asserted zero in every test.' Align the Implementation Guidelines bullet 'no write to any member'.

findings.text: The snapshot-size evidence covers the at-weld roster only. The 29.7 KB fixture (about 30.5 KB after T1, 4.6 percent headroom) is the loaded set at the weld. Rows are never removed: tombstones persist in the payload, RAGGED cuts append stub HULL_SEGMENT rows, cut seams keep their lists, and `defs` never shrinks. ADR-0013 § 6 permits one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. The lifetime-worst reachable state (every socket cycled once with RAGGED cuts, every queue at its bound, all defs interned) is therefore larger than the measured fixture, and no Validation item measures it. Separately, § 3.11's '32 KB is reached near 114 nodes' is at most 9 nodes away.
findings.amendment: Add a 'lifetime-worst' fixture to Validation and § 3.11: every socket welded and cut RAGGED once (ADR-0013 § 6 bound), queues at bound, maximal defs. Either show it fits under 32 KB or pre-commit lever 1 (the fluid-stamp side table) now, with the tradeoff stated. Cite ADR-0013's one-cycle-per-socket rule as the bound that makes tombstone growth finite at MVP.

findings.text: `GraphView`, the contract eight consumers code against, exists only as a prose list in § 9.1, with no Key Interfaces skeleton. Some reads that consumers need are absent from that list: a LOAD subtype getter for ADR-0028's fixture filter (TR-light-034 requires excluding non-Graph or self-powered fixtures and identifying lamp LOADs), a per-section compartment enumeration (TR-light-034's mean is per section, so a consumer must currently scan all compartments through `cid_at` and filter by `section_of`), and the descriptor-row getters of § 9.4, named only with ellipses.
findings.amendment: Add a `graph_view.gd` Key Interfaces skeleton with typed signatures and sentinel doc comments (T6) for every hot getter, including `load_subtype(id) -> int`, `compartments_in_section(section_id, out: PackedInt32Array) -> int` (ascending) and the full `desc_*` getter list. Tag each `## @hot` for the HOT-01 list.

findings.text: § 9.3 claims the descriptor store is sorted by construction, but the claim rests on unstated preconditions. The key is `(subject_kind << 40) | (subject_id << 8) | mode`, and the visit order is NODE, EDGE, COMPARTMENT, SEAM, OPENING. Strict ascent therefore requires the `GraphIds.SUBJECT_KIND` ordinals to be NODE < EDGE < COMPARTMENT < SEAM < OPENING, which is never pinned, and `ids.lock.json` would freeze whatever is written first. It also requires that OPENING edges are excluded from the EDGE pass, or that both passes cannot produce the same key, which is also unstated. The OPENING subject's anchor is undefined (the anchor bullet covers NODE, EDGE, COMPARTMENT and SEAM only).
findings.amendment: In § 4.7 or § 9.3, fix `SUBJECT_KIND` ordinals to the visit order (for example NODE 1, EDGE 2, COMPARTMENT 3, SEAM 4, OPENING 5). State that OPENING-kind edges are visited only in the OPENING pass. Define the OPENING anchor (for example `anchor_a` = edge id, `anchor_b` = -1).

findings.text: The Key Interfaces and internal text have drifted from each other and from ADR-0012. (a) The header's in-memory form is ambiguous: § 3.8 and the Implementation Guidelines say GraphState holds 'a Dictionary of int', while Key Interfaces declares `_h_*: int` members. The § 6.3 reflection allowlist differs between the two. (b) The `set_valve` snippet marks only EDGE and does not rebuild, but ADR-0012 § 6 says M8 changes connectivity, rebuilds and marks TOPO. Implementers copy snippets. (c) `GraphModule.setup` lacks ADR-0012's `work: WorkCounter`, the `graph.fail` stream registration and the ClockView source. (d) § 1 hard-codes 'divisor 6, offsets 0, 2, 4', where ADR-0012 makes both `GraphTuning` data. (e) `GraphFault.raise_ctx` mutates the caller's `detail` Dictionary.
findings.amendment: (a) Choose `_h_*` int members and state that the snapshot builds the hdr Dictionary. (b) Make the `set_valve` excerpt set `topo_dirty`, call `GraphDerived.ensure_derived`, and mark `EDGE` and `TOPO`, or cut it to a mutator that does not change connectivity (for example M10). (c) Adopt ADR-0012's `setup` signature. (d) Say 'divisor `tuning.graph_step_ticks`, offsets `tuning.hook_offset_*`'. (e) Copy `detail` before adding `subject`, or document the ownership transfer.

findings.text: Sibling ADRs have closed several items that ADR-0011 still carries open, and the Graph-side additions they ask for have not been adopted. Open Question 2 is closed by ADR-0016 (phase 0). Open Question 3 is closed by ADR-0012 § 7 (the EXOGENOUS clear rule). Open Question 8 and Risk 7 are closed by ADR-0012 § 8.2 (2-bit kind, 18-bit id), so § 4.1 (4) and § 8.4's '2^20 RNG subject field' becomes 2^18. Not yet adopted: `ONSET_UNKEYED` in the M1 check; `GraphIds.ALARM_CAPABLE_MASK`; the `GraphTuning` hook offsets, `load_queue_max`, `w_min_steps` and burst fields; the `GraphCaches` members `active_*`, `store_slots`, `machine_slots`, `exchange_links`, the POWER island list and `alarm_sections`; the `GraphDiag` counters `late_rebuilds`, `queue_dropped` and `footprints_clamped`; and the note that `FailureFilter.loaded_only` is always satisfied because the store holds loaded sections only.
findings.amendment: Mark Open Questions 2, 3 and 8 and Risk 7 as resolved, with pointers to the closing ADRs. Change 2^20 to 2^18 in § 4.1 (4) and § 8.4. Add a short 'Adopted from ADR-0012' list covering the GraphIds, GraphTuning, GraphCaches and GraphDiag additions, and require that `derived_members.json` includes them. Document `loaded_only` as retained for type stability and always true.

findings.text: Three smaller gaps. (a) § 4.6 describes the EMPTY state but not the ADR-0016 § 3.3 mechanism: `default_state(ctx)` must `ctx.put` a snapshot-shaped payload that the Graph's own `restore` accepts, and KRN-RST-07 tests that path. (b) After a restore of a store above a lowered `stock_cap`, readers and M16 `withdraw_store` see over-cap stock, and `stock_pm` can exceed 1000, for up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS - 1` ticks until the phase-0 reconcile; for a dormant section the window lasts until the section loads. Neither window is stated. (c) `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` (step 11) does not mention resolution through the ADR-0007 alias path, which ADR-0016 assumes. ADR-0007 defers aliases to a pre-SHIPPED story.
findings.amendment: (a) Add to § 4.6: '`default_state` builds this state as a payload with `GraphSchema` keys, `ctx.put`s it, and the kernel applies it through `GraphRestore.restore` (ADR-0016 § 3.3); the payload passes all § 7.2 steps.' (b) State in § 7.3 that `stock_pm` clamps to 1000 and that M16 may withdraw over-cap stock in the window, or forbid that, and give the dormant-section case. (c) Add to step 11: 'after `resolve_alias` once ADR-0007's alias story lands; the stored def string is not rewritten'.

findings.text: Gate items that pass: the problem statement and rationale are clear; alternatives 1 to 9 are genuinely considered; the Consequences section is honest (overlay readability, the indirection cost, no compaction, the 12x division cost); the engine is stamped as Godot 4.7.2 with Knowledge Risk MEDIUM; post-cutoff APIs (`@abstract` 4.5, typed Dictionary 4.4, both 4.7 GDScript rows) are flagged and probed on the editor binary, with the release-export gaps (S0-a/S0-b, S1, S3, LINT-SPIKE-1) named rather than claimed. TR traceability is complete: every row planned for ADR-0011 in requirements-traceability.md (TR-lsg-001..006, 018, 019, 024, 038; itemdb-014, 016, 031, 033, 040; instr-027; boarding-041; light-034; and the residuals of lsg-020, 022, 023, 030, 033 and itemdb-036) appears in a Decided-here or Owned-elsewhere table. The layout is right-sized for a determinism-critical solo MVP. The only addition beyond what Foundation required, `ids.lock.json` for persisted Graph enums, is a defensible zero-mechanism reuse of ADR-0007's ledger.
findings.amendment: None required. Optionally, state the right-sizing and spike-gating conclusion in the Review Log when the amendments land.
